```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Load required libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(caret)
library(pROC)
library(randomForest)
library(gbm)

# Custom colour palette
custom_palette <- c(
  "Logistic Regression" = "#1f77b4",
  "Random Forest"       = "#ff7f0e",
  "Gradient Boosting"   = "#9467bd"
)

# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(42)
```

1. Introduction
This document presents a comparative evaluation of three machine learning models — Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting — for predicting online shopper purchasing intention. The analysis uses the Online Shoppers Purchasing Intention dataset and focuses on model discrimination (ROC-AUC), classification performance, and practical implications for e-commerce operations.


Data Ingestion and Preprocessing

```{r }
# Load the dataset
# Make sure the path is correct relative to the location of this .Rmd file
df <- read.csv("../data/online_shoppers_intention.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Convert target to factor
df$Revenue <- factor(
  ifelse(df$Revenue == TRUE, "Purchase", "NoPurchase"),
  levels = c("NoPurchase", "Purchase")
)

# Separate target first
y <- df$Revenue
X <- df %>% select(-Revenue)

# One-hot encode only the predictors
dummies <- dummyVars(" ~ .", data = X, fullRank = TRUE)
X_encoded <- predict(dummies, newdata = X) %>% as.data.frame()

# Combine back
df_encoded <- cbind(X_encoded, Revenue = y)


```
3. Train / Test Split

```{r }
# Stratified 70/30 split
trainIndex <- createDataPartition(df_encoded$Revenue, p = 0.70, list = FALSE)
train_data <- df_encoded[trainIndex, ]
test_data  <- df_encoded[-trainIndex, ]

# Caret cross-validation control
train_control <- trainControl(
  method          = "cv",
  number          = 10,
  classProbs      = TRUE,
  summaryFunction = twoClassSummary
)

```
4. Model Training
```{r }
# 1. Logistic Regression
lr_model <- train(
  Revenue ~ .,
  data       = train_data,
  method     = "glm",
  family     = "binomial",
  metric     = "ROC",
  preProcess = c("center", "scale"),
  trControl  = train_control
)

# 2. Random Forest
rf_model <- train(
  Revenue ~ .,
  data      = train_data,
  method    = "rf",
  metric    = "ROC",
  ntree     = 100,
  trControl = train_control
)

# 3. Gradient Boosting
gbm_model <- train(
  Revenue ~ .,
  data      = train_data,
  method    = "gbm",
  metric    = "ROC",
  verbose   = FALSE,
  trControl = train_control
)
```
5. Model Evaluation

5.1 ROC Curves and AUC
```{r }
# Extract probabilities for the positive class ("Purchase")
lr_probs  <- predict(lr_model,  test_data, type = "prob")[, "Purchase"]
rf_probs  <- predict(rf_model,  test_data, type = "prob")[, "Purchase"]
gbm_probs <- predict(gbm_model, test_data, type = "prob")[, "Purchase"]

# Generate ROC objects
lr_roc  <- roc(response = test_data$Revenue, predictor = lr_probs,
               levels = c("NoPurchase", "Purchase"), direction = "<")
rf_roc  <- roc(response = test_data$Revenue, predictor = rf_probs,
               levels = c("NoPurchase", "Purchase"), direction = "<")
gbm_roc <- roc(response = test_data$Revenue, predictor = gbm_probs,
               levels = c("NoPurchase", "Purchase"), direction = "<")

# Print AUC values
cat("ROC-AUC Results\n")
cat(sprintf("Logistic Regression : %.3f\n", auc(lr_roc)))
cat(sprintf("Random Forest       : %.3f\n", auc(rf_roc)))
cat(sprintf("Gradient Boosting   : %.3f\n", auc(gbm_roc)))

```
```{r }

# Prepare data for plotting
extract_roc_df <- function(roc_obj, model_name) {
  data.frame(
    FPR   = 1 - roc_obj$specificities,
    TPR   = roc_obj$sensitivities,
    Model = model_name
  )
}

roc_df <- rbind(
  extract_roc_df(lr_roc,  "Logistic Regression"),
  extract_roc_df(rf_roc,  "Random Forest"),
  extract_roc_df(gbm_roc, "Gradient Boosting")
)

roc_df$Model <- factor(
  roc_df$Model,
  levels = c("Logistic Regression", "Random Forest", "Gradient Boosting")
)

# Create the plot (matching the Python version)
roc_plot <- ggplot(roc_df, aes(x = FPR, y = TPR, color = Model)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed",
              color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Logistic Regression" = "#1f77b4",
      "Random Forest"       = "#ff7f0e",
      "Gradient Boosting"   = "#9467bd"
    ),
    labels = c(
      sprintf("Logistic Regression (AUC = %.3f)", auc(lr_roc)),
      sprintf("Random Forest (AUC = %.3f)",       auc(rf_roc)),
      sprintf("Gradient Boosting (AUC = %.3f)",   auc(gbm_roc))
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Custom ROC Curve Comparison - E-Commerce Conversion Intent",
    x     = "False Positive Rate (1 - Specificity)",
    y     = "True Positive Rate (Sensitivity)",
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title        = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title        = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    legend.position   = c(0.72, 0.22),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "gray70"),
    legend.key        = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    panel.grid.major  = element_line(color = "gray90"),
    panel.grid.minor  = element_blank(),
    panel.border      = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.8)
  )

print(roc_plot)

# Save high-resolution version

ggsave("output/custom_roc_comparison_r.png", plot = roc_plot,
       width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 300)

```
5.2 Confusion Matrix and Classification Metrics (Random Forest)

```{r }

# Class predictions
rf_preds <- predict(rf_model, test_data)

# Detailed metrics
rf_cm <- confusionMatrix(rf_preds, test_data$Revenue, positive = "Purchase")
print(rf_cm)

# Visualisation
cm_df <- as.data.frame(rf_cm$table)
colnames(cm_df) <- c("Prediction", "Reference", "Freq")

cm_plot <- ggplot(cm_df, aes(x = Prediction, y = Reference, fill = Freq)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = Freq), fontface = "bold", size = 6) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#e8f4f8", high = "#1f77b4") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("No Purchase", "Purchase")) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = c("No Purchase", "Purchase")) +
  labs(
    title = "Confusion Matrix: Random Forest Classifier",
    x     = "Predicted Class",
    y     = "Actual Class"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13, hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    legend.position  = "none",
    panel.border     = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.8)
  )

print(cm_plot)

ggsave("output/custom_confusion_matrix_r.png", plot = cm_plot,
       width = 6, height = 5, dpi = 300)

```
6. Key Findings

Gradient Boosting achieved the highest discriminative performance (AUC ≈ 0.927), followed by Random Forest (≈ 0.915) and Logistic Regression (≈ 0.891).

Ensemble methods clearly outperform the linear baseline, indicating that purchasing intention is driven by non-linear interactions among behavioural features.

Random Forest shows strong precision on the minority class (Purchase) while maintaining excellent performance on the majority class (No Purchase).

The results support the use of ensemble models for prioritising high-intent sessions in marketing and operational decision-making.
